item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
[Image: A rectangle]

A. On the grid below, draw a rectangle whose length is three-fourths the length of the rectangle above, and whose width is two and one-half times the width of the rectangle above. Label the length and width of the new rectangle in centimeters on the figure. Each square on the grid is 1 cm by 1 cm.

[Image: A grid of squares]

descriptors: 6 cm and 5 cm. Rectangle is correctly drawn and labeled (on the figure).
Rectangle is correctly labeled, 6 cm and 5 cm, but drawing is incorrect.
Correct drawing is shown, but the length and/or width is not labeled or is incorrectly labeled.
One side is 6 cm and other side is incorrect, explicitly written or implicit from the drawing.
One side is 5 cm and other side is incorrect, explicitly written or implicit from the drawing.
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task). Also includes responses in which the drawing is missing.
Blank

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Triangular prism]

Which of these could be folded to make a shape like the 3-D figure above?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Net with three rectangles connected in a V-shape by two triangles]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Net with three stacked rectangles and two triangles on the right]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Net with three rectangles and three triangles]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Net with three stacked rectangles, one triangle on the top right and one triangle on the bottom left]

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem shows a 3-D triangular prism resting horizontally on one rectangular face, with dashed lines indicating the three hidden edges. The options show four candidate nets:
- Option A: A central horizontal rectangle with an isosceles triangle attached to each vertical side, and another rectangle attached to the outer edge of each triangle angled upward, forming an open V-shape.
- Option B: Three congruent rectangles stacked vertically in a column, with two identical triangles attached to the right edges of the top and middle rectangles, both pointing right.
- Option C: Two congruent rectangles stacked vertically, each having a triangle attached to its left edge pointing left; a third rectangle extends to the right from the top rectangle, ending with a triangle pointing right.
- Option D: Three congruent rectangles stacked vertically in a column, with one triangle attached to the right edge of the top rectangle pointing right, and another triangle attached to the left edge of the bottom rectangle pointing left.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Which of these could represent the expression 2x + 3x?

options.label: A
options.text: The length of this segment: [Image: X and 5 are segment lengths on a number line, and the segment length of 5 is slightly larger than the segment length of x.]

options.label: B
options.text: The length of this segment: [Image: 2, 3, and x are segment lengths on a number line. The segment length of 2 is the smallest. The segment length of 3 is around twice the length of 2, and the segment length of x is almost three times the length of 2.]

options.label: C
options.text: The area of this figure: [Image: A rectangle, where one side of the rectangle is labeled “x” and the other side is divided, with the smaller part labeled 2, and the larger part other labeled 3.]

options.label: D
options.text: The area of this figure: [Image: A rectangle, with one side is labeled 5 and the other side is divided in two equal parts, with each part labeled with “x”.]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four options showing visual representations:
- Option A shows a horizontal line segment with vertical tick marks at its ends, divided into two segments by an interior vertical tick mark. The segment on the left is labeled x above, and the segment on the right is labeled 5 above.
- Option B shows a horizontal line segment with vertical tick marks at its ends, divided into three segments by two interior vertical tick marks. From left to right, the segments are labeled 2, 3, and x above.
- Option C shows a rectangle with its left vertical side labeled x. A vertical dotted line extends through the rectangle, dividing the top horizontal side into two parts, labeled 2 on the left and 3 on the right.
- Option D shows a rectangle with its left vertical side labeled 5. A vertical dotted line extends through the rectangle, dividing the top horizontal side into two equal parts, each labeled x above.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Rectangle ABCD containing two tangent circles P and Q]

In the figure above, ABCD is a rectangle, and circles P and Q each have a radius of 5 cm. What is the area of the rectangle?
reference_items.figure_description: A rectangle ABCD is oriented horizontally with vertices labeled A at the top-left, B at the top-right, C at the bottom-right, and D at the bottom-left. Inside the rectangle are two identical circles labeled P and Q, with their centers marked by dots labeled P and Q. The two circles are tangent to each other horizontally at the midline of the rectangle. Circle P touches the left side AD, the top side AB, and the bottom side CD. Circle Q touches circle P, the right side BC, the top side AB, and the bottom side CD. A vertical line segment is drawn from center P up to the point of tangency on top side AB, labeled "5 cm".

reference_items.figure_description:
Three geometric figures composed of small congruent right triangles:
- Figure 1: A single square with a diagonal line from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner, dividing it into two right triangles labeled '1' (top-left) and '2' (bottom-right). Below the square is the label 'Figure 1'.
- Figure 2: A square divided into a 2-by-2 grid of 4 smaller squares. Each smaller square has a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, creating 8 congruent triangles numbered 1 through 8: top-left square has 1 (upper) and 2 (lower); top-right square has 3 (upper) and 4 (lower); bottom-left square has 5 (upper) and 6 (lower); bottom-right square has 7 (upper) and 8 (lower). Below is the label 'Figure 2'.
- Figure 3: A square divided into a 3-by-3 grid of 9 smaller squares. Each smaller square has a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, creating 18 congruent triangles. None of the triangles are numbered. Below is the label 'Figure 3'.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

step1.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's step 1 parameter d1? In the GPCM, b - d1 is the ability at which earning the first point becomes more likely than earning no point, so a higher d1 means that this point is earned at a lower ability; the steps sum to 0. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
